attributes.summary: The conventions lock moves from the version folder to the contract surface. A version directory now holds ontology.md and nothing else; readme.md, principles.md, librarians/ and skills/ move to unversioned exfu/ and travel with plugin releases. Deciding rule, mechanically decidable: a file belongs in a version directory if and only if a Follows: line can anchor into it. Measured -- all 16 Follows: anchors point into ontology.md. Supersedes the open question left by conventions-versioning-timestamps (may a shipped base be edited in place: no). Decision doc at planning/conventions-lock-boundary.md.
Refines the timestamp scheme rather than replacing it: that note governs how the identifier churns, this one governs what the identifier covers.

Al, 2026-07-24 in session: approved the diagnosis and the split, then 'Write it up as a plan and then do it'. Timing ruled by him -- 'only I break' this week, clients onboard next week, so break and fix now.

attributes.text: Reject 'additive-only writes' to a shipped convention base; fix the lock boundary instead. Three reasons. (1) The base is read live -- agent-registry.json pins agents to definitions by versioned path -- so an additive line in a librarian's writes: frontmatter is textually additive but expansive in authority. (2) The additive-is-safe intuition comes from schemas whose consumers ignore unrecognised fields; agents ignore nothing. (3) 'Byte-identical' is checkable in CI, 'additive enough' is judged by whoever wants the edit -- and v0.3 was patched in place three times, each presumably locally reasonable. Also: the identifier would stop being a sufficient description of a content set.

attributes.summary: 0.8.0 shipped first, base untouched: dashboard.html at the library root, written by dashboard-generator.py. A redirect page, not a symlink -- sync layers handle symlinks unreliably (same reason exfu/latest.txt is a text file), and browsers resolve relative URLs against the document URL, so a symlinked page would break the dashboard's own ../../../scopes/... gallery links and view iframes. Idempotent (unchanged pointer not rewritten, so nightly runs don't churn mtime through the sync layer) and refuses to overwrite a dashboard.html it did not author.

0.9.0: base minted as 20260724-1749 holding ontology.md alone; readme/principles/librarians/skills moved to unversioned exfu/. Root-layout depiction moved out of the ontology to exfu/readme.md. The two 0.8.0 edits that were blocked are folded in. New build/check-conventions-lock.sh (run by build.sh before composing) and build/mint-conventions.sh. Install skills, migrate skill, substrate guide v11, exfu-library, exfu-guides and the wow template all describe the split shape. Registry source paths stop breaking on every mint.

attributes.text: Google Cloud's Open Knowledge Format (published 2026-06-12, v0.1): align now, adopt natively later, interoperate by projection. Recorded in principles.md. Deliberately NOT done: no field renames (name/title, purpose/description would break the index parser, dashboard, every template and every installed library at once -- a migration, not an alignment), no isolated type: field (ceremony without the rest of conformance), and no one-concept-per-file -- that contradicts the v7 flattening of the ontology into a single file because agents ingest one complete read far more reliably, which Follows: anchoring depends on. Interop needs an importer and a generated projection, both additive.

attributes.summary: A convention for updating an installed library over time. Migrations are boot-detected rather than scheduled (a plugin update does not touch the library, so there is no update hook to fire); durable state lives in a new top-level ledger/ that no plugin refresh touches; migration ids are timestamps so lexicographic order is application order. Closes the gap left by conventions-lock-boundary: no standalone upgrade path existed for an already-installed library. Decision doc at planning/library-migrations.md.
That note drew the line between frozen and evolving; this one governs how a library crosses it.

Al, 2026-07-24: 'proceed with creating a plan for this migrations work and then execute', with three rulings supplied in the same message -- migrations should not be scheduled agents, durable state should move out of exfu/ to its own top-level folder, and a new conventions version is appropriate.

attributes.text: Three rulings from Al that shaped the design, all corrections to the initial sketch. (1) Migrations are NOT scheduled agents: a plugin update changes what is installed alongside the library, not the library, so no hook can fire at update time; detection moves to boot, execution is user-consented. Auto-update and the Claude Code/Cowork split make this sharper -- the same library can be opened by two surfaces on different plugin versions, so a library AHEAD of its surface must be detected and block structural work. (2) The ledger moves out of exfu/ to a top-level ledger/: exfu/ is refreshed wholesale on update and exfu/derived/ is a disposable cache, while the ledger is the one thing that cannot be regenerated. Named ledger/ rather than _state (the underscore convention was retired with _meta/ and _trash/). (3) Mint a new conventions version for it.

attributes.summary: Minted 20260724-1831 carrying the ledger location (#ledger) and the migration concept and format (#migrations). Shipped exfu/librarians/library-updater.md, exfu/migrations/ with the first migration (20260724-1831-split-convention-base), and ledger templates. Boot detection added to exfu-library as Step 7 covering all three hazard cases; install seeding added to all three install skills; substrate guide v12. Skill wiring delegated to two subagents in parallel and verified independently rather than on report.

Two defects found and fixed by testing, both of which would have shipped. (1) mint-conventions.sh rewrote historical identifiers in the changelog: grep -r emits src//shared/... with a doubled slash, silently defeating the literal path guard on history-recording files. It corrupted the v0.9.0 entry on the first real mint; paths are normalised now and the entry was restored byte-identical. (2) exfu-migrate-to-dropbox would have destroyed the ledger -- it copies whole roots and refreshes exfu/, with no carve-out for the one directory that cannot be regenerated. Carve-out added, plus ledger/ in both top-level structure enumerations.

Third defect, found by executing the migration end to end: its applies_when tested for the PRESENCE of the old shape, but step 3 deliberately preserves old version directories, so the condition stayed true forever and would re-trigger on every check of a library with no ledger. Inverted to test for the ABSENCE of what the migration produces, which is false once it has run. Generalised into the ontology as a rule for authoring any migration precondition, since the same trap applies wherever a migration leaves the old shape readable.

attributes.text: Migration preconditions are written as the absence of what the migration produces, not the presence of what it replaces. Migrations routinely leave the old shape in place (superseded convention versions stay readable for scopes pinned to them), so a presence test never becomes false. Recorded in ontology #migrations rather than only fixing the one migration.

attributes.summary: Reopened on Al's design correction, before release: the top-level `ledger/` is too specific a name for a root entry, because more stateful things will need to survive outside exfu/ over time (he named long-lived databases and SQLite). The container becomes the category, with the ledger as its first tenant.

attributes.text: Top-level `durable/` replaces top-level `ledger/`, which moves to `durable/ledger/`. Name chosen on evidence via a judge panel, not taste: the corpus already used the word 'durable' for exactly this category in ten places written before anyone tried to name a folder, and it pairs against `derived` so the rule states itself -- derived is rebuilt, durable is kept. `state/` was rejected as actively unsafe: the ontology already points that word at the cache ('Current state belongs in the derived index'), so a root `state/` would make the one file every agent reads cold contradict itself. Membership is an iff with three required conditions (unregenerable, about-the-library, append-only text), where the third excludes SQLite and binaries by construction -- which matters because libraries sync through Dropbox or git, where database sidecars sync out of order and two surfaces produce unmergeable conflicted copies. So the SQLite that prompted the generalisation does not itself belong in the container.

The refresh carve-out is stated positively and never as an exception list: 'a refresh replaces exfu/; it never touches durable/, user/, or scopes/'. An exception list grows silently wrong as durable tenants are added, and a forgotten entry destroys the only category of file that cannot be recovered. This is the general form of the data-loss bug found in exfu-migrate-to-dropbox in the previous commit, and it is why the container earns its place at all: one container means one carve-out, permanently.

The unreleased 0.10.0 changelog entry was revised in place rather than superseded by an 0.11.0, and the guide's v12 and v13 entries folded into one, since both described the same unreleased release.

Worse in general -- libraries record migration ids in their ledger, so every future mint would have silently orphaned those records and made applied migrations look pending, reintroducing the exact failure the seeding rule exists to prevent. The script now preserves `id:` lines under exfu/migrations/ while still moving `conventions:`, and the invariant is stated in the ontology.

attributes.text: A migration's id is its own authoring identity and never tracks a conventions mint; its `conventions:` field moves freely because that records the movement the migration performs, not what the migration is. Recorded in the ontology rather than only fixed in the script.

attributes.summary: Enactment of release 0.11.0 carried out in one working tree: conventions minted as 20260903-1743 with the ontology rewritten around docket/ (three folder-types deprecated in place; new #docket-mechanics: records, mixins, triggers, signals, fires, actors, channels, grants, schedule modes, dispatcher; derived-location rule corrected; scope-by-scope migration journal rule); docket templates and one docket-template.md replacing the reminders/inbox pair; librarians backlog-sweep, docket-compact, dispatcher and a revised library-updater contract; registry template with the hourly cadence; new stdlib library-index/index.py (incremental SQLite+FTS5 index outside the synced root, due view, receipts, signals, compaction) with a 56-check self-test; substrate-index and dashboard-generator taught the docket with labelled legacy paths; exfu-library, scope-setup, new setup-docket, daily-briefing, the three install skills, install-scheduled-agent, the hourly task prompt, guides, substrate guide v14, primers and the fetch-model migration updated; migration 20260903-1743-docket written (offered per scope, journalled, reversible); example library converted (user/ to a docket with legacy/, a granted Slack DM channel, Acme deliberately left deprecated); manifests bumped to 0.11.0 and the changelog entry written; plugins/ rebuilt. Work split across four background sub-agents plus the orchestrator; an independent review found one real bug (a receipt invocation missing its root argument in the shipped template), fixed.

attributes.command: python3 build/test-library-index.py
attributes.summary: 56 checks pass: rebuild idempotence, exact one-row upsert and delete, FTS query, cron in Europe/London with weekend gap, once not due early, disarm on delivered, signal emission, on-signal fires once, claim visible to a second actor, due.json served then refused when stale, conflicted-copy fold, archive with kind, entry-completed emitted once, nothing binary under the root.

attributes.command: ./build/build.sh all
attributes.summary: All three plugins build at 0.11.0: conventions lock passes with 20260724-1910 reported as superseded by a mint, manifests valid, every SKILL.md frontmatter valid.

attributes.command: substrate-index/index.py example; library-index/index.py rebuild|due example; dashboard-generator.py example
attributes.summary: Example library indexes four scopes with docket and deprecated fields; the due view finds the two overdue reminders and resolves slack-dm to auto via the grant; the dashboard regenerates and, opened in the browser, shows the Docket tab with Tasks (docket ClickUp pointer, Acme deprecated pointer, Q3 renewal deprecated checkboxes) and Reminders bucketed overdue/later. No sqlite, wal or shm files anywhere under the library root.

attributes.reason: Needs a live attended session on a real pre-0.11 library and a phone with the Dropbox connector; the example was converted by hand following the migration's steps, not through the library-updater flow.
attributes.summary: Owed: the first real run of migration 20260903-1743-docket through library-updater on a pre-0.11 library (Al's own is the natural first), and the connector-path check of reading and rewriting docket/reminders.jsonl from a phone and seeing the next desktop boot pick it up.

structured-worklist enacted as release 0.11.0 (conventions 20260903-1743): the docket, mixins, triggers, signals, receipts, channels, grants, the dispatcher and the per-machine index all shipped; old folder-types deprecated in place and the migration offered per scope. Two real-world verifications deferred and recorded. Marketplace entry bump lives in ExFu/exfu-marketplace and is not part of this repo.
